pr_title: x86: start pcie in early init level.
pr_body:
Move PCIe to EARLY and UART to pre-kernel level.

Fixes various bugs where uart driver was started too late (in
post-kernel).

Fixes #62761
Fixes #62717

Signed-off-by: Anas Nashif <anas.nashif@intel.com>
pr_comments:
Just to summarize, we have the following dependency graph on any platform that enables ACPI and has its UART as a PCIe device:

ns16550 -> PCIe -> ACPI

AFAIK, one reason why ACPI is POST_KERNEL is that ACPICA depends on the libc heap (malloc) being available. I'm not sure if I looked at the right place, but based on `lib/libc/common/source/stdlib/malloc.c` it looks like the libc heap is indeed initialised only at POST_KERNEL level at least in some build configurations:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/d8b153e00f06d8b9943da3d477afc2c5d8fad250/lib/libc/common/source/stdlib/malloc.c#L263
So, to be able to move all these things earlier one would either need to eliminate the malloc dependency, or then initialize the libc heap much earlier.

@najumon1980 does the above seem like a correct assessment? Did I miss or misunderstand something?

> AFAIK, one reason why ACPI is POST_KERNEL is that ACPICA depends on the libc heap (malloc) being available.

hmm, I do not see ACPI in post kernel, i.e. when building for ehl or rpl

> > AFAIK, one reason why ACPI is POST_KERNEL is that ACPICA depends on the libc heap (malloc) being available.
> 
> hmm, I do not see ACPI in post kernel, i.e. when building for ehl or rpl

Najumon has PRs in review

Actually, I was wrong: after looking at the ACPICA Zephyr adaptation code it's using `k_malloc()` and *not* `malloc()`. `k_malloc()` in turn seems to use this heap:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/e364f29bffdfb122fead4b7dad082428f2f6969c/kernel/mempool.c#L61
I.e. it looks like that should be immediately available. In that case this whole assumption of ACPICA needing POST_KERNEL is incorrect, i.e. we might be able to move PCIe and ACPI simply early enough (like this PR is trying to do).

> Actually, I was wrong: after looking at the ACPICA Zephyr adaptation code it's using `k_malloc()` and _not_ `malloc()`. `k_malloc()` in turn seems to use this heap:

if acpi and those depend on it need to be in post kernel, that is a major problem IMO. 
The original code was putting pcie in pre kernel and pushing uart to post maybe because we were not getting the priorities right or whatever in one single init level which is a workaround that does break things, i..e how can you have uart in post kernel and uart console (depdending on uart device) in pre kernel?

> > Actually, I was wrong: after looking at the ACPICA Zephyr adaptation code it's using `k_malloc()` and _not_ `malloc()`. `k_malloc()` in turn seems to use this heap:
> 
> if acpi and those depend on it need to be in post kernel, that is a major problem IMO. The original code was putting pcie in pre kernel and pushing uart to post maybe because we were not getting the priorities right or whatever in one single init level which is a workaround that does break things, i..e how can you have uart in post kernel and uart console (depdending on uart device) in pre kernel?

ACPI is not only dependent on HEAP memory, but other factor like it need more stack than what available in pre-kernel (where it use interrupt/exception stack instead of main stack). I will debug further this issue in ACPI context and update you.

> ACPI is not only dependent on HEAP memory, but other factor like it need more stack than what available in pre-kernel (where it use interrupt/exception stack instead of main stack). I will debug further this issue in ACPI context and update you.

I'd assume that the early (interrupt?) stack size is configurable, and the platforms that use ACPI have plenty of memory, so it should be possible to just increase it.

I created following PR as an alternative (ns16550 UART related issue) for this PR to fix issues:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/64473

@nashif , looks the up_squared board currently using in your val is very old and our customers might not use currently. So it will great if you are able to upgrade to latest Upsquared board which is based on Alder Lake N (which we already enabled support). You can find board details: https://up-shop.org/default/ups-pro-7000-series.html

The issue with ACPI root caused: ns16550 driver init hung if configure as PRE_KEREREL_1 is due to HPET timer init priority (PRE_KEREREL_2) which is lower than ns16550. This is because acpi internally use sys_clock_cycle_get_64 and this cause issue since HPET was not insatiate at the time. Any way this issue will to happen with latest mainline code due to recent change to use apci_tsc timer as system timer. I also provided following PR: https://github.com/acpica/acpica/pull/905 which will remove existing acpi DSDT API limitation and can be use in PRE_KEREREL_1 as well.

Your this PR can be merge and will not break existing ADL platform.

this is the most relevant line:
`DEVICE: ASSERTION FAIL [device_is_ready(uart_dev)] @ WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/subsys/logging/backends/log_backend_uart.c:127`

Someone, (@najumon1980?) has changed init levels and we now have uart console start before the uart driver. Also, it seems we have uart driver come up in post kernel, which is very bad.

review_comments: Seems like qemu_cortex_a53 does not like this change.
yeah, more dependency hell
btw, still not sure what was the problem the original code was trying to solve.

and it seems the proposed solution here https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/64022 will not work, i.e, if we move pcie back to pre_kernel:

> and it seems the proposed solution here #64022 will not work, i.e, if we move pcie back to pre_kernel:

Yes, it's the neverending issue of the non-direct relationship with  DTS/Kconfig/Zephyr init entries.
I mean, as long as we cannot have all in one place (dts nodes + "software" nodes + Kconfig tweaks) to generate a proper init dependency tree, we are doomed to mangle the level/prio manually. Tough one
I don't think there are any other users of `CONFIG_UART_NS16550_PARENT_INIT_LEVEL` so you should probably remove its definition in the same go.

the change introducing this Kconfig and the change in init levels already broke few platforms. This fixes the issue, so please verify before assuming it will break anything else and please confirm that the tests exposing this issue work for you as well without this change.
